objective: Measure the pointwise rank of the tensor basis on the actual duct baseline fields before the tensor-basis rung is scored a priori on them, and say how much of the anisotropy the representation can reach at all
rationale: Derived from Pope 1975 and checked to machine precision this session. A linear eddy viscosity RANS solve on a straight duct produces exactly zero secondary flow, which this lab already measured, so its mean field is unidirectional and its velocity gradient has one non-zero row. On such a field the ten basis tensors have pointwise rank exactly three, not five: singular values 5.474, 3.448, 2.235 and then 5.8e-16 and 3.1e-16, a clean gap. The fifth and tenth tensors are identically zero, so two of the ten coefficients have no effect. And a two-dimensional subspace of the symmetric traceless tensors cannot be produced by any values of the ten coefficients whatsoever, one of whose directions has zero streamwise row and column to 4.7e-16, a pure cross-plane tensor of the family this lab already names as b_yz and b_yy minus b_zz. The approved duct generalisation item specifies an a priori gate, beating the baseline on anisotropy RMSE against a held-out LES field, and that gate would be scored inside a representation that is rank three out of five at every cell. This is not an argument against the rung. Fed back into a solver the prediction generates secondary flow and the degeneracy disappears, so it is a property of the first iterate. It is an argument that the a priori number means something different from what it appears to mean, and that the difference is measurable in advance at no compute.
gate: For each duct training case, the pointwise rank of the ten tensors and the fraction of the true LES anisotropy lying outside their span is computed per cell and reported as a distribution, and any a priori anisotropy RMSE the rung reports is printed beside the best RMSE the representation could achieve at that rank
cost_basis: estimate; reads duct fields already on disk and does linear algebra on 3x3 tensors per cell. The comparable audit, closure_duct_anisotropy_expressivity.py, measured 41,971 cells in 17.3 seconds on a 2-core cap
expected_knowledge_gain: An a priori score against a rank-deficient representation cannot be read as model quality until the floor set by the rank is on the page beside it
citations: Pope, JFM 72 331 to 340, 1975, p. 334, READ IN FULL 2026-08-02
in_sample_verdict: Clean, and it tightens rather than loosens the existing boundary. It reads only the four duct TRAINING cases the correction model already trains on, AR_1_Ret_180, AR_3_Ret_180, AR_5_Ret_180 and AR_10_Ret_180, exactly the scope the existing duct expressivity audit declared. The validation case AR_7_Ret_180 and the three scored test cases AR_1_Ret_360, AR_3_Ret_360 and AR_14_Ret_180 are never opened, and no score call is made. It fits nothing: the rank of a basis is a property of the baseline field, not of any model.
